inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: Q2 2026 diluted weighted-average ordinary shares 5,894M (6-K ex99.1, 2026-08-25) / 4 ordinary shares per ADS = 1,473.5M ADS. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows (charging both would double-count). Basic count at the same date is 5,627M ordinary = 1,406.8M ADS.
inputs.ads_ratio: 1 ADS = 4 ordinary shares (stated in every PDD earnings release)
inputs.cash_composition: June 30 2026: cash & equivalents 128,918 + short-term investments 327,496 (= company's own 'cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments' RMB456.4bn) + non-current held-to-maturity debt securities 70,296 (Dec-31-2025 20-F figure; the June split of 'other non-current assets' 96,383 is not disclosed, so the 12.6bn of non-current AFS securities at Dec-2025 is deliberately left OUT as a cushion against the ~8bn decline in that line). EXCLUDED: restricted cash 77,274 (merchant float), equity-method investments, receivables from payment platforms. Convertible notes (5,309.6 at Dec-2024) were repaid in FY2025 (RepaymentsOfConvertibleDebt 5,228.7); borrowings are nil. Lease liabilities 4,844 excluded from debt under lease treatment (B).
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 20-F cash-flow add-back (us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensation = AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense, RMB7,936.971m). PDD discloses no cash tax paid on net-share settlement of equity awards (no tag, no financing line), so the combined figure equals the add-back. H1 2026 SBC was RMB2,831m (1.30% of revenue) vs RMB4,129m in H1 2025.
inputs.buyback_note: PDD has never repurchased shares (no PaymentsForRepurchaseOfCommonStock in any 20-F) and pays no dividend. The flat ADS count is therefore a modelling convention the company has not paid for in cash; in practice the diluted count has drifted from 5,714M (FY2021) to 5,894M (Q2 2026), +0.7%/yr, which the full SBC expense is the charge for.
inputs.capex_note: us-gaap:PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment is tagged only through FY2020 (43.0). FY2021-25 capex is DERIVED from the PP&E-gross roll-forward: FY2025 5,800.5 - 4,804.7 = +995.8 -> RMB1,000m used (0.23% of revenue); FY2024 +585; FY2023 +598; FY2022 +458. D&A FY2025 601.5 (0.14%). The Metrics CSV CapEx column is blank for FY2021-25 for this reason.
inputs.fx_note: Model -> quote: 1 CNY = 0.14928 USD, i.e. USD/CNY 6.6987 (Yahoo CNY=X, 2026-10-01). Parity check: Q2 2026 6-K converts at 6.7850 (Fed H.10, 2026-06-30), so the RMB has firmed ~1.3% since; the 6-K's US$16.56bn for RMB112,358m revenue reproduces that rate (112,358 / 16,560 = 6.785). No dual listing exists for a direct price parity check (PDD has no HK line). All per-ADS values are computed in RMB and multiplied by fx_rate; the unsuffixed intrinsic_value / weighted_iv are in USD to match current_price.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in the flows' currency (CNY): China 10y CGB ~1.9% + beta 1.2 x (mature-market ERP 5.5% + China country premium ~1.5%) = ~10.3%, used as 10.0% across all three scenarios. Regulatory, tariff and delisting risk is carried in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked on the rate (adaptations rule f). This is 0.5pp below the 10.5% USD-tech house default: the RMB risk-free rate is ~2.5pp below USD, partly offset by the higher ERP.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) leases as operating cost. US GAAP ASC 842 operating-lease expense is already inside PDD's operating costs, so reported operating income / EBITDA is post-lease; no principal is deducted from the flows and lease liabilities (RMB4,844m at June-2026) are excluded from net debt. Right-of-use amortisation is inside the 0.15% D&A line, so cash-tax EBIT is not double-charged. Leases are immaterial (ROU assets 0.7% of total assets).
inputs.nci_treatment: None required: non-controlling interests are immaterial (net income attributable to ordinary shareholders equals net income in every period).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component route, 10-year horizon. PDD is an asset-light consumer-internet marketplace (advertising + transaction commissions) with no debt and a very large net-cash pile; the routing table's first row applies, plus the adaptations file for (a2) RMB flows against a USD quote and (b) leases. NOT a mid-cycle FCF case: FY2025 owner FCF (RMB72.4bn) is neither a peak nor a trough on the component build (FY2024 90.9bn was the peak, inflated by a 30% adjusted-EBITDA margin that the price-war/regulatory environment has since compressed to ~23%). What IS unusable is the historical growth rate - 49% revenue CAGRs are a Temu-launch artefact - so the forward path is anchored to the H1 2026 run rate (revenue +9.5%, Q2 +8%, GAAP operating margin 21.7%, adjusted EBITDA margin ~23%) and management's explicit H2-2026 margin-pressure commentary, not to any CAGR. INTEREST INCOME: RMB25.6bn (24% of OCF) is stripped from the FCF base because the RMB527bn cash pile is added at face (net cash is ~7x the FCF base). Stripping gross pre-tax interest while the cash-tax rate is applied to EBIT is slightly conservative. TRAPPED-CASH: see valuation_philosophy - net cash alone is ~RMB357/ADS (~US$53/ADS at fx_rate), ~70% of the market price, and the market is plainly not paying face for it. A 10% PRC dividend-withholding leakage on the RMB150.6bn of undistributed PRC-subsidiary earnings disclosed in the FY2025 20-F is deducted in equity_bridge as the identifiable cost of repatriation. DATA FLAG for the parser: PDD_Metrics.csv's Currency column says USD but every value is CNY (FY2025 revenue 431,845.7 = RMB431.8bn; the 20-F's US$ convenience figure is 61,753). Should be corrected via make fix. Also the two 'Q3 2019'/'Q3 2020' rows are equity-only strays from the XBRL feed.

equity_bridge.item: PRC dividend withholding tax on undistributed PRC-subsidiary earnings (10% x RMB150,575.9m, FY2025 20-F DeferredTaxLiabilitiesUndistributedForeignEarnings disclosure)
equity_bridge.note: The identifiable cash leakage between the consolidated cash pile and an ADS holder. The 5% treaty rate would halve this; 10% is the statutory rate and the conservative choice.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: H1-2026 run rate (+9.5% YoY, Q2 +8%) fading toward 3% terminal; equals the average of the base path's first five years
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Every historical CAGR (revenue 49%, equity 52%, EPS 41%, owner FCF 26%) is a FY2021-24 Temu-launch artefact and is not a forward rate; FY2025 revenue growth was already 9.7% and H1 2026 9.5%. Equity CAGR exceeds owner-FCF CAGR by 2x because retained earnings include RMB20-26bn/yr of interest income on the cash pile. EPS 5-year CAGR is undefined (FY2020 EPS was -1.51).
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF CAGRs are computed on OCF - capex (PP&E-gross derived) - SBC - interest income: FY2020 22,086; FY2021 20,946; FY2022 36,193; FY2023 76,246; FY2024 90,892; FY2025 72,418. Owner-FCF 3yr CAGR (26.0%) sits well below reported-FCF 3yr CAGR (30.3%) because interest income has grown 6.4x since FY2022 while operating cash generation grew 2.2x; an increasing share of reported cash flow is treasury yield, not operations. FY2025 owner FCF fell 20% from the FY2024 peak on the margin reset.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +8% = H1 actual (+9.5%) with Temu's EU volumes slowing into the EUR150 threshold removal; fades 1pp/yr to mature Chinese-ecommerce growth of 3-4% by year 6.
base.margin_rationale: Adjusted (pre-SBC) EBITDA margin: FY2024 30.2%, FY2025 23.5%, H1 2026 23.1%. Management guided continued pressure in H2 2026 (RMB100bn merchant program, R&D +40%), so 23.0% -> 22.5% for FY2026-27, then a partial recovery to 24% as the program rolls off - deliberately well below the FY2024 peak because Beijing's June-2026 'rat race' intervention caps take-rate expansion.
base.tax_rationale: FY2025 cash taxes paid 21.6bn vs pre-tax 119.4bn = 18.1%, but ~6bn of that is tax on interest income which this model strips; the operating cash rate is ~16.5%. Ramped to 22% as PRC high-tech preferential rates (15%) roll toward the 25% statutory rate and more profit shifts offshore to Temu.
base.wc_rationale: Merchant-payable float grows with GMV: 5% capture on the revenue increase (FY2023 was 22%, FY2024/25 ~0%; 5% is a cautious midpoint).
base.cap_rationale: 14x terminal FCF: below the 20x house default because this is a price-war-exposed, policy-exposed Chinese ADR that today trades at ~3x owner FCF ex-cash. Gordon at 10%/3% would be 14.7x, so the cap binds marginally.

scenario_narratives.base: Pinduoduo holds share in a low-single-digit-growth Chinese e-commerce market while Temu rebuilds on local/semi-managed fulfilment after the US de-minimis loss and the EU threshold removal; consolidated revenue grows 8% in FY2026 fading to 3%. The RMB100bn merchant program and trust-and-safety R&D keep the adjusted EBITDA margin at ~23% through FY2027, after which it recovers only to 24% - Beijing's June-2026 intervention against subsidy and price competition caps take rates well below the FY2024 peak of 30%. SBC stays ~1.5% of revenue, cash tax drifts from 19% to 22%, and the cash pile is added at face less 10% PRC withholding leakage.
scenario_narratives.bull: Temu's geographic diversification (Europe ~45% of GMV, Latin America, Middle East) more than offsets the US reset and the local-fulfilment model reaches scale, keeping revenue growth at 10% for two years before fading. The merchant program ends on schedule, R&D intensity normalises, and the adjusted EBITDA margin climbs back to 28% by year 7 - still below FY2024. Regulators stay quiet, the HFCAA overhang eases via a Hong Kong listing, and the company begins returning cash, which the market then prices nearer face; the terminal cap is 16x.
scenario_narratives.bear: The EU follows the US in removing its duty-free threshold, Temu's European economics are impaired as badly as its US ones were, and domestic regulators force Pinduoduo to unwind subsidy-led promotions while Alibaba, JD and Douyin keep competing on price. Revenue stalls for four years (5%, 2%, 0%, -2%) and the adjusted EBITDA margin falls to 15% as the merchant program is extended and preferential tax rates lapse (cash tax 25%). Working-capital float stops growing. The terminal cap is 9x. Note that even this path sits above the current price because ~70% of the market cap is net cash; the bear case for the equity is really the trapped-cash and delisting case described in valuation_philosophy, which the flows cannot express.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 30% because PDD depends on two regulators it cannot influence - Beijing on price/subsidy competition and Washington on tariffs, de minimis and HFCAA - and the Temu pivot to local fulfilment is an unproven re-engineering of the model that made the growth. Bull cut to 20% because it needs several independent things to go right at once: Temu EU resilience, domestic margin recovery, regulatory calm, and a start to cash returns. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: An owner-FCF DCF on PDD is two valuations stapled together: an operating business generating ~RMB72bn of owner FCF after stripping RMB25.6bn of treasury interest, and a RMB527bn cash and securities pile worth ~RMB357 (~US$53) per ADS on its own at the model's FX rate. The market price covers the cash pile and leaves the operating business at roughly 3x owner FCF, which is the clearest statement of what the market believes: that this cash will not reach ADS holders at face (no dividend or buyback in the company's history, PRC capital controls and 10% withholding on repatriation, HFCAA delisting risk, VIE-structure governance). The house method adds net cash at face, so every scenario including the bear lands above the price. Read the result as: the operating business is cheap on any reasonable margin path, and the upside hinges almost entirely on whether and when the cash is returned or credibly re-rated. A memo value that haircuts the net cash by 50% (deduct ~US$27/ADS from each scenario's intrinsic value) is the more honest 'trapped-cash' reading and is what the price is nearest to. Terminal values are capped at 14x base / 16x bull / 9x bear FCF, all above today's ~3x ex-cash multiple, so the valuation assumes a re-rating of the operating business; the required-return table shows what the price implies without it.
key_risks_to_valuation: Trapped cash: ~US$53/ADS of the intrinsic value is net cash the company has never distributed; if it is never returned, the realisable value is nearer the 50%-haircut memo figure.

US-China policy: EU de-minimis removal (after the US one in May 2025) would hit Temu's largest region; further tariff or parcel legislation would compress the transaction-services line that is now ~half of revenue.
Domestic regulation: Beijing's June-2026 summons over 618 subsidies signals that take-rate expansion back toward the FY2024 30% margin is politically unavailable; the base case assumes only 24%.
HFCAA / delisting: the ADS could be barred from US trading; a Hong Kong listing is a mitigant but not yet in place.
Capex and D&A are derived (PP&E-gross roll-forward), not reported; the error is at most ~0.2% of revenue.
FX: a 5% RMB depreciation lowers every USD value by 5%; the rate is dated and must be refreshed with the price.
